scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Look at this! It connects to a monitor!

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Wow! Did you build this yourself?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes. I worked on it for months.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: This is really cool. Show me more.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: You can type and see text on screen.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I think people would buy this.
scripts.hint: '~을 살 것 같아'에서 추측을 나타낼 때 would buy를 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Really? Who would want a computer?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Hobbyists and tech fans. There's a market.
scripts.translated: 취미로 하는 사람들이랑 기술 좋아하는 사람들. 시장이 있어.
scripts.hint: '취미로 하는 사람들'은 Hobbyists로, '기술 좋아하는 사람들'은 tech fans로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: But I made it just for fun.
scripts.translated: 근데 난 그냥 재미로 만든 건데.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Let's start a company. Trust me.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Okay. Let's try it together.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Look at this board. It's a real computer.
scripts.hint: '~을 좀 보세요'는 Look at으로 시작하여 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Interesting. What can it do?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It runs programs. It's easy to use.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I like it. I'll order fifty units.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Fifty? That's wonderful!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: But only if they're fully assembled.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: We can do that. When do you need them?
scripts.hint: '가능합니다'는 We can do that으로 자연스럽게 표현할 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Within thirty days. What's your wholesale price?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: $500 wholesale, $666.66 retail. Deal?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Deal. See you in thirty days.

topics.title: 외상 거래의 기술
topics.partner: 전자부품 가게 점원 해럴드 모리슨 (직원, 남성, 40대)

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I need electronic parts for a project.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Sure. What do you need?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Here is my list. But I have no cash.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Sorry, we don't give credit here.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Look at this. It's from Byte Shop.
scripts.translated: 이거 보세요. Byte Shop에서 온 거예요.
scripts.hint: '~에서 온 거예요'는 It's from으로 간단하게 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Byte Shop? What is this paper?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: A real order. Fifty computers.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Fifty computers? That's a lot.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I can pay in thirty days. Please trust me.
scripts.translated: 30일 안에 갚을 수 있어요. 저 믿어주세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Okay. I'll help you this time. Good luck.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Thank you for meeting me today.
scripts.hint: '시간 내 주셔서'는 for meeting me로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Sure. Tell me about your computer project.
scripts.translated: 그럼요. 컴퓨터 프로젝트에 대해 얘기해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: We want to put a computer in every home.
scripts.translated: 저희는 모든 가정에 컴퓨터를 보급하려고 합니다.
scripts.hint: '~에 보급하다'는 put ~ in으로, '모든 가정'은 every home으로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Every home? How big is the market?
scripts.translated: 모든 가정이요? 시장 규모가 어느 정도죠?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Millions of families could buy one.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: What makes your computer special?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It's easy to use and affordable.
scripts.hint: '가격이 저렴하다'는 affordable이라는 형용사 하나로 표현할 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: How much money do you need?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: We need $250,000. I'm ready to start.
scripts.hint: 금액을 말할 때 '~이 필요해요'라는 의미로 We need를 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'll invest $250,000 and help manage. Call tomorrow!
scripts.translated: 25만 달러 투자하고 경영도 도와드리죠. 내일 연락 주세요!

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: The investment is done. We need a name.
scripts.translated: 투자는 끝났어. 이제 이름을 정해야 해.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes, we do. Any ideas?
scripts.translated: 그러게. 뭐 생각해 둔 거 있어?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: How about "Apple Computer"?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Apple? Why an apple? It's strange.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Apples are friendly and innovative.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: But it doesn't sound like technology.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: That's why people will remember it.
scripts.hint: '그래서 ~하는 거지'라는 표현은 That's why로 문장을 시작해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Hmm. Any other reason for Apple?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It comes before Atari in phone books.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: That's clever! Okay, Apple Computer it is.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Welcome to my studio. How can I help?
scripts.translated: 스튜디오에 오신 걸 환영해요. 뭘 도와드릴까요?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I need a logo for my company.
scripts.hint: '회사를 위한'이라는 의미로 for my company를 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Sure. What kind of design do you want?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: An apple. But with a bite taken out.
scripts.translated: 사과요. 근데 한 입 베어문 느낌으로요.
scripts.hint: '한 입 베어문'은 a bite taken out으로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: A bitten apple? That's an interesting idea.
scripts.translated: 한 입 베어문 사과요? 재미있는 아이디어네요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes. Simple but memorable. That's the goal.
scripts.translated: 네. 단순하면서도 기억에 남게. 그게 목표예요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I understand. Color or monochrome for this?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Color. I want it friendly and innovative.
scripts.hint: '~하게 하고 싶어요'는 I want it 뒤에 형용사를 붙여 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Great choice. Bright colors will stand out.
scripts.translated: 좋은 선택이에요. 밝은 색이 눈에 띌 거예요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Perfect. I trust your creative vision here.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'll start today. See you soon.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Welcome to the Apple booth!
scripts.hint: '~에 오신 걸 환영합니다'는 Welcome to로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Thanks! Is this a personal computer?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes, this is the Apple II.
scripts.hint: 특정 제품을 가리킬 때는 정관사 the를 붙여 the Apple II로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Is it a finished product?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes, in a plastic case.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: How do I use it?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Just connect a monitor.
scripts.hint: '~만 ~하면 돼요'라는 의미로 Just를 문장 앞에 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Can it show color graphics?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes! Games and programming too.
scripts.translated: 물론이죠! 게임도 하고 프로그래밍도 할 수 있어요.
scripts.hint: '게임도... 프로그래밍도'에서 반복되는 '~도'를 and... too 구조로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: This is the future. Thank you!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Hello! Who are you? You look young.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I'm Steve Jobs. I'm twenty-two years old.
scripts.hint: 나이를 말할 때 '~살이에요'는 years old로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Twenty-two? And you have your own booth?
scripts.translated: 스물두 살이요? 그런데 직접 부스를 운영하시는 건가요?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes. My company is called Apple.
scripts.hint: '이름은 ~이에요'라는 표현을 is called로 바꿔서 문장을 만들어 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: How did you start this company?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: My friend and I started in a garage.
scripts.hint: '친구랑'을 주어로 표현할 때 My friend and I를 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: What are your plans for the future?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I want computers in every home.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Do you think young people can do big things?
scripts.translated: 젊은 사람들도 큰일을 해낼 수 있다고 생각하세요?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes. Age doesn't stop good ideas.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Great story! Thank you and good luck!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Welcome to Xerox PARC. I'll show you our work.
scripts.translated: 제록스 파크에 오신 걸 환영합니다. 저희 작업물을 보여드릴게요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Thank you. What will you show me?
scripts.hint: '뭘 ~할 건가요?'라는 질문은 What will you로 시작해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: This is a new way to use computers.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: What is that small box there?
scripts.hint: '저기 저'는 that과 there를 함께 사용하여 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It's called a mouse. I use it to click.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: You click on those small pictures?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes, they're icons. Each one opens a window.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: This is the future! Can we use this?
scripts.translated: 이게 미래야! 우리도 이걸 쓸 수 있을까요?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: You mean for your company's computers?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes! I will put this in our next computer.
scripts.translated: 네! 다음 컴퓨터에 이걸 넣을 겁니다.
scripts.hint: '~에 넣을 겁니다'는 will put this in으로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: That's ambitious. I wish you the best.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Steve, the board made a decision today.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: What decision? Tell me.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: They decided to remove you from management.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Remove me? I built this company!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I know. But the sales are very low.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: The Macintosh will sell. Give it time.
scripts.hint: '시간을 주세요'는 Give it time이라는 표현을 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: The board doesn't want to wait anymore.
scripts.translated: 이사회가 더 이상 기다릴 생각이 없대요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: This is my company. My dream.
scripts.hint: '여긴 ~예요'는 Here is가 아닌 This is로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: This is a business decision. Not personal.
scripts.translated: 이건 사업적인 결정이에요. 개인적인 게 아닙니다.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I understand. This is very hard.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I know. I'm sorry it ended this way.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: So, here we are. Our new beginning.
scripts.translated: 자, 드디어 여기까지 왔군. 우리의 새로운 시작이야.
scripts.hint: '드디어 여기까지 왔군'은 here we are라는 표현으로 나타낼 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes, but Apple filed a lawsuit.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I expected that. They kicked me out.
scripts.translated: 예상했어. 날 쫓아낸 게 그 사람들인데.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Will we be okay?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes. They can't stop us from working.
scripts.translated: 그럼. 우리가 일하는 걸 막을 순 없어.
scripts.hint: '~가 일하는 걸 막다'는 stop ~ from working 구문을 활용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: What will NeXT do?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: We'll make computers for the education market.
scripts.translated: 교육 시장을 위한 컴퓨터를 만들 거야.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Better than Apple?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Much better. Let's prove it together.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I followed my heart. Let's get to work.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: What is your dream for this team?
scripts.hint: '이 팀을 위한'이라는 의미로 for this team을 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We want to make 3D animated movies.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Movies made by computers?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes. Computers can create new worlds.
scripts.translated: 네. 컴퓨터로 새로운 세계를 창조할 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Five million dollars is a lot of money.
scripts.hint: '큰돈'은 a lot of money로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It is. But this technology is very valuable.
scripts.translated: 그렇죠. 하지만 이 기술은 정말 가치가 있습니다.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Technology and art together. That's interesting.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We plan to make a feature film soon.
scripts.translated: 저희는 곧 장편 영화를 만들 계획입니다.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I will invest. Let's do great things.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Thank you! We won't let you down.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: You wanted to see me. What's this about?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Apple wants to buy NeXT.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Just my company? Or something more?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I need your help too. Please come back.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: How is Apple doing right now?
scripts.hint: '~의 상황이 어떻습니까?'를 How is ~ doing으로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Honestly, not good. We are losing money.
scripts.translated: 솔직히, 좋지 않습니다. 적자가 나고 있습니다.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I see. I have some conditions.
scripts.hint: '알겠습니다'는 I see로 간단하게 표현할 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Of course. What do you need?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I need to decide on the products. That's all.
scripts.translated: 제가 제품을 결정해야 합니다. 그게 전부입니다.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I agree. Welcome back to Apple.
scripts.translated: 동의합니다. 애플에 다시 오신 걸 환영합니다.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I have a new idea for Apple.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Great. What is the idea?
scripts.hint: '아이디어'는 the idea로 표현하여 질문을 완성해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: The campaign is called 'Think Different.'

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Think Different? I like that name.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We use pictures of great innovators.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Which people will you show?
scripts.hint: '어떤 사람들'을 물을 때 Which people로 문장을 시작하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Einstein, Picasso, Gandhi, and more.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: That's perfect. This is Apple!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We can use TV and print ads.
scripts.translated: TV랑 인쇄 광고로 할 수 있어요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I approve. Start right away.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Thank you! Apple will rise again.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: What about a translucent plastic case?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: That's revolutionary! I love it.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It will look friendly and modern.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Make it all-in-one. Use only USB ports.
scripts.hint: '~으로 하다'는 Make it으로 표현하고, '~만'은 only로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: No floppy drive? That's very bold.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: People don't need floppy disks anymore.
scripts.translated: 사람들 이제 플로피 디스크 필요 없어요.
scripts.hint: '이제 ~없어요'라는 의미를 표현할 때 문장 끝에 anymore를 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We can offer many colors too.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Colors? What do you have in mind?
scripts.hint: '~을 생각하고 있다'는 have in mind라는 표현을 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Bondi blue first, then five more later.
scripts.translated: 본다이 블루로 먼저 시작하고, 나중에 다섯 가지 더 추가하죠.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: This will bring Apple back. I'm sure.
scripts.hint: '~을 되살리다'는 bring back이라는 표현을 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We're making history. I'll start right away.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I have an idea for a music player.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Tell me about it.
scripts.hint: '~에 대해'라는 의미의 about it을 활용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It uses a small hard drive inside.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: How many songs can it store?

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: About one thousand songs.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: One thousand songs in your pocket!

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: But battery life and size are problems.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: The user experience must be perfect.
scripts.hint: '~해야 해'라는 필수/의무의 의미는 must be로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: What features do you want?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: A scroll wheel. iTunes sync. Let's do this.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Thank you. I'll start right away.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Is the team ready?
scripts.hint: '준비 됐어?'라고 물을 때 Is... ready?라는 구조를 사용하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes. Everything is ready.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Good. Let me practice one more time.
scripts.hint: '~해볼게'라는 의미를 Let me로 시작하여 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Of course. I'm listening.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: An iPod. A phone. An internet device.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes. And they are one device now.
scripts.translated: 네. 그리고 이제 그게 하나의 기기죠.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: We call it the iPhone.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: That's great. The message is clear.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It's time. I'm going on stage now.
scripts.hint: '무대에 올라가다'는 go on stage로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Good luck. This is a historic moment.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: The iPad design is finally complete.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Let me see it.
scripts.hint: '~해 보자'라는 표현은 Let me로 시작해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Here it is. Very thin and light.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Perfect. Not a PC or a phone.
scripts.hint: '~도 ~도 아니야'는 영어로 Not... or... 구조를 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It's right between them. A new category.
scripts.translated: 딱 그 사이에 있죠. 새로운 카테고리입니다.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: How much does it weigh?
scripts.hint: '무게가 나가다'는 동사 weigh를 사용해서 질문을 만들어 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: One and a half pounds only.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It should feel like holding a book.
scripts.translated: 책 들고 있는 것처럼 느껴져야 해.
scripts.hint: '~것처럼 느껴지다'는 feel like로, '들고 있는'은 holding으로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We designed it for comfort.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Let's launch it. A new era begins.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: The tablet market starts with iPad.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Come in. Please sit down.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Of course. Is something wrong?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I have to tell you something.
scripts.hint: '할 말이 있다'는 have to tell이라는 표현을 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'm listening.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: My health is getting worse.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'm so sorry. What can I do?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I want you to become CEO.
scripts.hint: '~해줬으면 해요'라는 바람은 want ~ to 구문으로 표현하세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Me? Are you serious?

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Yes. Please take care of Apple.
scripts.hint: '~을 부탁해요'는 take care of라는 표현을 사용해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I will continue your vision.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It's me. Tomorrow is the big day.
scripts.hint: '중요한 날'은 the big day라는 표현으로 나타내 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Yes, we're almost ready here.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Please emphasize Siri. It's very important.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: Siri will be the main demo.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Voice AI is the future of computers.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I understand. It's a big change.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Ask Siri different questions on stage.
scripts.translated: 무대에서 Siri한테 여러 가지 질문 해봐.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'll show how Siri talks naturally.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Good. This will change everything. Thank you.
scripts.translated: 좋아. 이게 모든 걸 바꿀 거야. 고마워.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: We'll make it great. Take care.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: It's getting harder to breathe now.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'm right here. I love you.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: You and the kids are my best work.
scripts.hint: '최고의 작품'은 my best work로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: You changed the whole world.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: I hope Apple continues to innovate.
scripts.hint: '계속 혁신하다'는 continues to innovate로 표현해 보세요.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: It will. You built something amazing.
scripts.translated: 그럴 거예요. 당신은 대단한 걸 만들었잖아요.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: Tell the kids I love them.

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: They know. They're right outside.

scripts.speaker: A
scripts.english: The light... Oh wow... so beautiful...

scripts.speaker: B
scripts.english: I'll love you forever. Rest now.
